reason: Fewer than two of the screens we link have a maker-stated fit range that includes 13 inches on a page opened today, and the table cannot reach four sourced rows. The one that qualifies is the FOPO S788 (12–18.5-inch, FOPO's range, from our record). The Duex Plus DS, the true pick and not yet a record, has a maker statement only for the earlier 'Duex Plus': Mobile Pixels' blog of 2023-06-28 says 'Duex Plus is designed for 13-14" laptops with a screen size of 13.3" FHD'. The page that reportedly states 13–14 inches for the DS (mobilepixels.us/collections/duex-series) returned HTTP 429. Mobile Pixels' own blogs put the Duex Max at '14" or larger', so our Duex Max DS is outside the question. FOPO's fit ranges for the S1 and S7 were not read: fopomonitor.com product pages returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, fopodisplay.com returned 403, and the store search returns only the first ~1,500 characters of the listing (CSS). No rival row could be priced today: sidetrak.com returned 502 and amzcheck was blocked by Amazon. I used 30 tool calls against the budget of about 25.
why_angle: Recommended for a re-run: the cited rivals (itechguides, lbdsoftware) warn that MacBook limits vary but give no display count per chip. Angle C has Apple's own counts for M1, M2, M3 (lid closed only) and M4/M5, all opened, and they are why one added screen is the pick. Angle D reaches the same finding but rests its M1 figure on Plugable.
sourced_for_rerun: Duex Plus (13.3-inch) fit, Mobile Pixels' words: 'designed for 13-14" laptops'; 'Weighing 1.3 lbs'. Duex Max: 'perfect attachment for laptops with 14" or larger displays', 1.8 lbs, 300 nits. Blog dated 2023-06-28, read 2026-11-21. It names the Duex Plus and Duex Max, not the DS versions.
Duex Max: 'It is perfect for laptops that are 14" or larger', 'weighs only 1.8 lbs'. Blog dated 2023-08-07, read 2026-11-21.

Duex Plus DS manual (2023 V1): 13.3 in, weight 1.8 lbs, thickness 0.60 in (thinnest 0.35 in). One USB-C to C cable on a port with DP Alt Mode; USB-C plus HDMI on a port without it; USB-A adapter plus HDMI on laptops with only USB-A and HDMI. No laptop fit range ('use the DUEX Plus DS with recommended display size of your laptop'). Read 2026-11-21 through a PDF-to-text reader (r.jina.ai), which reported the spec table as garbled. The 1.8 lb conflicts with the roughly 1.3 lb in ChatGPT's first answer and for the earlier Duex Plus, so re-read the PDF directly before printing a weight.

Duex DS Series store listing: 13.3-inch (Duex Plus DS) or 14.1-inch (Duex Max DS); USB-C and Mini HDMI 'without the need for drivers or software'; magnetic and sliding design; from $183.99 (list $299.99), in stock. Store search read 2026-11-21. Angle D read the variants: Plus DS $183.99, variant id 42717917904962; Max DS $215.99, variant id 42717909876802.

Mobile Pixels comparison tool: a 14.1-inch dual-screen column shows 1.8 lbs, 8.9 × 12.6 × 0.25 in, 250 nits, FHD. Columns are not labelled by model in the text read, so it is not usable as is. Read 2026-11-21.
FOPO S7 store search, read 2026-11-21: $199.99, list $499.99, in stock. No fit range in the text returned.
unsourced: Mobile Pixels' fit range for the Duex Plus DS by name: a search result summary says mobilepixels.us/collections/duex-series lists 13–14-inch laptops for the Plus DS and 14-inch and larger for the Max DS; the page returned HTTP 429 and was not opened.

FOPO's laptop fit range, weight and Mac statement for the S7: a search result summary says fopomonitor.com lists 12–17.3 inches and fopodisplay.com 13–16 inches with lid limits (length 10–14.6 in, height above 8.27 in, thickness under 0.28 in); neither page opened (429 and 403).

Duex Plus DS body width and height: the Mobile Pixels spec page angle A read (12.25 × 8.46 in) is for the earlier Duex Plus.

rerun_when: Once mobilepixels.us and fopomonitor.com stop returning 429, read (1) mobilepixels.us/collections/duex-series or the Duex DS product page for the DS fit ranges and weights, and (2) the FOPO S1 and S7 product pages for FOPO's laptop size range. If the S1 or S7 states 13 inches, the page has four linked rows (Duex Plus DS as a new cj:mobilepixels record at $183.99, FOPO S1, S7 and S788) and can be written on angle C with the Duex Max DS named as left out, just over the line by Mobile Pixels' own '14" or larger'.
